MARKET.head: Oatley family buys Rosemount, Ingoldby and Secret Stone from Treasury Wine Estates
MARKET.summ: Treasury Wine Estates (TWE) has announced the sale of the Rosemount, Ingoldby and Secret Stone brands to A.G. Oatley Wines, owned by the Oatley family. The company said the sale is the latest step in its transition to a more focused brand portfolio, following its recent sale of the Seppelt, Rouge Homme and Tollana brands to local owners.
takeaways: Treasury Wine Estates is selling its Rosemount, Ingoldby and Secret Stone brands to A.G. Oatley Wines, owned by the Oatley family.
The sale is part of TWE's plan to cut its 76 brands to a priority portfolio of 30.
The transaction is expected to complete on 23 October 2026, with TWE keeping European Rosemount sales rights for up to three years.

MARKET.head: Fiano planting and listings spread across Australia ahead of Fiano Day
MARKET.summ: With Fiano Day around the corner (Friday 16 October), Daily Wine News took a trip to the McLaren Vale and sat down with Corrina Wright, winemaker and director at Oliver’s Taranga Vineyards, to learn more about the alternative white that’s causing quite the buzz. Last year, Oliver’s Taranga Vineyards worked with Mastermind...
takeaways: Corrina Wright of Oliver's Taranga Vineyards in McLaren Vale says Australia has about 300 Fiano producers, up from an estimated 80.
Royal Adelaide Wine Awards chair of judges Samantha Connew said Fiano entries rose from seven to 43 in 2026.
Fiano Day falls on Friday 16 October, with Oliver's Taranga launching a trade page so wineries can download event assets.

MARKET.head: VINITECH-SIFEL 2026 in Bordeaux to host 700 exhibitors and 40,000 wine professionals
MARKET.summ: From 1-3 December 2026, Bordeaux will welcome wine professionals from around the world for VINITECH-SIFEL, a leading international trade show dedicated to innovation and solutions for the wine, fruit and vegetable sectors. Bringing together 700 exhibitors, 40,000 professionals from 70 countries and 70,000 m² of exhibition...
takeaways: VINITECH-SIFEL, a wine, fruit and vegetable trade show, runs 1-3 December 2026 in Bordeaux with 700 exhibitors.
The show expects 40,000 professionals from 70 countries across 70,000 square metres of exhibition space.
International Buyers Program offers eligible investors 4-star hotel stays and travel cost support, with free registration for technical visits.

MARKET.head: Treasury Wine Estates cuts 170 jobs as new operating model nears
MARKET.summ: According to reporting by The Australian, Treasury Wine Estates (TWE) has axed 170 roles as part of its previously announced major operational and regional restructure. The article details that the redundancies are mostly across roles in marketing, IT, finance and support roles at TWE’s offices. The Australian said that some...
takeaways: Treasury Wine Estates has cut 170 roles, mostly in marketing, IT, finance and support at its offices, per The Australian.
Most redundancies are at the Melbourne headquarters and other offices, though some are believed to have hit vineyards.
The restructure creates a simplified portfolio and a new operating model effective 1 October 2026, with recruiting continuing for commercial roles.

MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA debuts in New York City at Pier 36 in October 2026
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA, organized by Veronafiere with the Italian Trade Agency, holds its first New York City event at Pier 36 on October 26-27, 2026.
After two years in Chicago, the event will host 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 labels, its largest exhibitor count to date.
A 95-winery delegation organized by the Italian Trade Agency joins regional collectives from Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Lazio and Sardinia; registration is open.

MARKET.head: Global wine demand shifts from red toward white and sparkling styles
MARKET.summ: The global wine industry has been undergoing a significant structural transformation. While declining overall wine consumption has attracted considerable attention, another important trend has emerged beneath the surface: a steady shift in consumer demand from red wine towards white and sparkling wine.
takeaways: IWSR data shows red wine's share of global consumption fell from about 52% in 2012 to 43% in 2025.
Over the same period, white wine rose from 31% to 34% and sparkling wine from 8% to 13%.

MARKET.head: Australian wine exports to Malaysia, Indonesia and Philippines grow despite shifting markets
MARKET.summ: Southeast Asia is an increasingly important region for Australian wine exporters seeking to diversify and build new markets. Population growth, rising household incomes and increasing consumer interest in premium imported beverages are supporting opportunities across the region although market maturity, consumer preferences,...
takeaways: Wine Australia export data for the year to June 2026 show Australian wine exports to Malaysia up 30 per cent in value to A$55 million.
Indonesia exports rose 300 per cent in value to A$21 million, while Philippines exports fell slightly to A$11.5 million.
IWSR 2025 data rank Indonesia, Philippines and Malaysia as the fourth, fifth and sixth largest wine markets in ASEAN.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads Liv-ex trade with 33% share; DRC dominates Burgundy
MARKET.summ: In this week’s Talking Trade, US buyers maintained their lead of purchasing, with EU buyers behind increasing their purchased value by 140% week-on-week
takeaways: Bordeaux took 33.0% of traded value on Liv-ex this week, with the 2009 and 2019 vintages the top-traded by value.
Burgundy placed second with 28.5%, and Domaine de la Romanee-Conti accounted for over a third of its trade.
Champagne fell to 13.9% of traded value from 21.4% last week, while US buyers took 47% of regional purchasing by value.

MARKET.head: Liv-ex says fine wine market stabilising, with recovery starting at the top
MARKET.summ: Tom Burchfield, Head of Decision Intelligence at Liv-ex, presented at the Drinks Business Conference 2026 on the state of the fine wine market
takeaways: Liv-ex's Fine Wine 1000 index is back to its 2015 level in real terms, per presenter's conference talk.
Q3 Liv-ex trade value rose steeply versus Q2 2026 and Q3 2025, with demand returning at the top end.
Pre-2011 Bordeaux trade rose sharply on Liv-ex in Q3, a sign buyers are re-engaging.

MARKET.head: WineGB launches Scandinavian tour for English and Welsh wine exporters
MARKET.summ: WineGB confirms Scandinavian tasting tour, creating a high value commercial opportunity for members. WineGB confirms its Scandinavian Trade & Media Tasting Tour, a three city showcase across Stockholm, Oslo and Trondheim, designed to accelerate export growth for English wine producers and deliver meaningful commercial value for...
takeaways: WineGB's Scandinavian Trade & Media Tasting Tour visits Stockholm, Oslo and Trondheim, featuring over 20 English and Welsh producers.
In 2024, 14 of 16 producers showing in Stockholm secured new listings or new market business.
English wine export sales grew 9% in 2024, with volumes up 35%, across 50 countries.

MARKET.head: Vineyards can earn SFI payments for cover crops and habitat, if actions suit the business
MARKET.summ: The second application window for the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) is set to open on 22 September, so Hutchinsons head of environmental services, Georgina Wallis, highlights some actions that may be of interest to growers in the viticulture sector. While the SFI is primarily aimed at arable and livestock farms, vines and...
takeaways: The Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) 2026 includes vines and horticultural permanent crops, with 71 actions, several relevant to vineyards.
LEAF Marque Standard version 17.0 requires 5% of farm area as habitat, with an optional 10% advanced target.
The RPA uses satellite imagery to monitor SFI action delivery, and overwinter cover crops should ideally be sown by late August or early September.

MARKET.head: Seven proposed US AVAs spanning California to New Jersey seek federal wine region recognition
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven proposed American Viticultural Areas, from California to Minnesota and New Jersey, are seeking TTB approval, a process that can take several years.
The proposed Annapolis-Sea Ranch AVA would cover 26,637 acres with 651 acres of grapes across a dozen vineyards, within the West Sonoma Coast AVA.
The 723,760-acre Deschutes River AVA would be the first recognized winegrowing region in central Oregon, proposed by the Central Oregon Winegrowers Association.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup previews Southern Glazer's probe, Maker's Mark releases and more
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. It was a quiet week on the news front, but as we gear up for gifting season, there are a ton of new product drops.
takeaways: California has launched an investigation into Southern Glazer's Wine and Spirits over a reported bribery issue.
Trump is reported to be lifting the tariff on Irish whiskey, and Scottish distillers are responding to a new English single malt category.
GunBun has filed for bankruptcy, and Stateside is in a legal dispute with AB InBev.

CULTURE.head: Seven oaky, buttery Chardonnays that balance richness with bright acidity
CULTURE.summ: Chardonnay has long been one of the world’s most popular wine grapes. Though it originated in Burgundy, the variety is now grown across every major wine region, and as it spread, many different vinification styles emerged. Despite its versatility, Chardonnay became synonymous with the heavily oaked, buttery style from...
takeaways: Wine site list of seven oaky, buttery Chardonnays that balance richness with crisp acidity, aimed at drinkers avoiding the 1990s butter-bomb style.
Picks include Concannon Reserve (Livermore Valley, 14.1 percent alcohol) and Rombauer 2024 Carneros, a longtime big-style American Chardonnay.
Other picks range from Soter Estates (Willamette Valley) and Domaine Serene Evenstad Reserve (Dundee Hills, aged 13 months) to Garden Creek and St. Innocent Enchanted Way.

CULTURE.head: Tom Surgey and Henry Jeffreys to host Vineyard Show masterclass tribute to Matthew Jukes
CULTURE.summ: This year’s masterclass, always a highlight of the Vineyard & Winery Show, will be held as a tribute to wine writer and former masterclass host Matthew Jukes following his sad death on 6 August this year. The tribute will be led by renowned wine experts Tom Surgey and Henry Jeffreys. The masterclass at the Kent
takeaways: Wine writers Tom Surgey and Henry Jeffreys will co-host the Vineyard & Winery Show masterclass at Kent County Showground as a tribute to Matthew Jukes.
Jukes, a wine writer and former masterclass host, died on 6 August; ticket proceeds go to the Drinks Trust charity, as he did.
Surgey and Jeffreys are also new Vineyard magazine columnists, and the show will present a new Matthew Jukes Trophy for Wine of the Year.

CULTURE.head: Wolf Blass named 2026 South Australian Legend of the Vine by WCA
CULTURE.summ: Wine Communicators of Australia (WCA) announced Wolf Blass AM as the 2026 South Australian ‘Legend of the Vine’ on Friday (9 October) at the Royal Adelaide Wine Awards Lunch. The SA Legend of the Vine Award is presented by Wine Communicators of Australia to “recognise a South Australian who is of excellent character, who is...
takeaways: Wine Communicators of Australia named Wolf Blass AM the 2026 SA Legend of the Vine on 9 October at the Royal Adelaide Wine Awards Lunch.
The award honours South Australians of excellent character who have contributed to Australian wine and share WCA's values on communicating about wine.
In 1967 Blass introduced a colour-coded tiered label system (Grey, Yellow, Red, Black, Platinum) to make wine easier for everyday drinkers to understand.

CULTURE.head: Saumur's Bouvet-Ladubay marks 175 years of Loire sparkling winemaking
CULTURE.summ: Set your navigation southwest from Paris and follow your wine-loving heart to the Loire. There, along the curving river’s central stretch, you’ll find the country’s third-largest wine region: a verdant, chateau-studded valley where waves of vines give birth to grapes destined for an effervescent future.
takeaways: Bouvet-Ladubay, founded in 1851 in Saumur by Etienne Bouvet and Célestine Ladubay, is celebrating its 175th anniversary this year.
The producer, the largest maker of méthode traditionnelle sparkling wine in Saumur, operates eight kilometres of cellars carved from former limestone quarries.
Its Cuvée blends Chenin Blanc, Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc from around 80 winegrowers, with wines exported to about 50 countries.

CULTURE.head: Bartenders say American drinkers abroad are curious, though they still favor vodka
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: European bartenders at London's Connaught Bar and Madrid's Rosewood Villa Magna describe American bar guests as curious, open and conversational.
Americans often order vodka Martinis and customized classics, and request American spirit substitutions at European bars.
U.S. visitors reached a record 24 million trips to Europe in 2025, per The Wall Street Journal.

SCIENCE.head: Analysis of vineyard irrigation water shows how its minerals help or harm soils
SCIENCE.summ: THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. Part Two of a Three-Part Vineyard Mineral Nutrient Management Lab Analysis Series.
takeaways: Nearly pure snowmelt-fed water strips minerals from soils, making them more acidic, less fertile and less permeable over time.
Saline well water and high sodium adsorption ratio can damage vine foliage and soils, especially under drip emitters.

SCIENCE.head: Newsletter gathers vineyard resilience research, cover crop guides and regenerative recognition
SCIENCE.summ: Our September newsletter is out. This month: Tasting Climate Change 2026 sessions now available to watch; practical guides on cover crops, weed management and compost teas; fresh research on resilience and economics in regenerative vineyards from France to Sonoma, plus new recognition for ROC and regenerative producers from...
takeaways: Canavera et al. (2026, Environmental Microbiome) found under-vine cover crop mulching in a non-irrigated Piacenza, Italy vineyard raised microbial diversity and cut pathogen pressure.

A 2026 Field Crops Research study of Mediterranean rainfed vineyards found roller-crimped cover crops improved soil cover, vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization without hurting grape quality.
The same study found seasonal climate, not management, was the dominant driver of fungal diversity.

SCIENCE.head: French wine harvest set to fall 14% below recent average after heatwaves
SCIENCE.summ:
This year’s harvest expected to be down 2% on mediocre yield in 2025, when production was lowest in nearly 70 years

France’s wine industry is facing a historic low harvest after the country was hit by a series of summer heatwaves.

At about 35m hectolitres, the total harvest would be down 2% on a mediocre 2025...
takeaways: France's 2026 harvest is estimated at about 35m hectolitres, down 2% on 2025 and 14% below the 2021-2025 average.
Champagne harvested early in September for the first time, with output halved from last year as extreme heat sped sugar buildup.
Burgundy and Beaujolais production is projected 30% below the five-year average, while Bordeaux is expected to rise 10% on 2025.

SCIENCE.head: Emeritus Vineyards shifts to dry farming and sells grapes to partner wineries
SCIENCE.summ: Emeritus Vineyards in California stays focused on quality and pursues new opportunities in a difficult wine market
takeaways: Emeritus Vineyards in Sebastopol, California, began a four-year transition off irrigation starting in 2007, dry farming its vines.
The change reportedly improved wine quality and flavor and made vines more resilient to September heat events.
Emeritus begins harvest seven to 10 days before neighbors and also sells a meaningful share of its fruit to winery partners.

SCIENCE.head: Hampshire firm Wildflower Co. shortlisted for South Coast tech award
SCIENCE.summ: Hampshire-based biodiversity specialist Wildflower Co. is a finalist in the South Coast Tech and Innovation Awards, in recognition of its groundbreaking use of science and technology to help tackle biodiversity loss and accelerate nature recovery. The pioneering company, which combines more than two decades of scientific...
takeaways: Hampshire biodiversity specialist Wildflower Co. is a finalist in the South Coast Tech and Innovation Awards' Tech for Good category.
Its Meadowscape Pro system can establish high-quality meadow habitats in three to four months.
The company also sells its Meadow in a Bag product to homeowners through its Wild Gardens brand.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Galiza: a seminar focusing on the wines of Galicia, Spain
NEWSLETTERS.summ: For the 2026 edition of Simplesmente Vinho the guest region was Galiza (Galicia) in Spain, and there were nine visiting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Winefeed's 2026 Simplesmente Vinho featured Galiza (Galicia) as guest region, with nine visiting producers and a seminar hosted by Miguel Anxo Besada and Antonio Portela.
The seminar tasted wines from five Galician appellations: Ribeiro, Rías Baixas, Ribeira Sacra, Valdeorras and Monterrei.
Luis Anzio Rodríguez's Viña de Martin 2015 Ribeiro scored 96/100, the highest score in the tasting, with Zarate El Palomar 2021 Rías Baixas at 95/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting a Bit of California Wine History
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I had the good fortune last week of being invited to the home of a wine collector in San Francisco
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: A San Francisco wine collector hosted the author for a tasting of California wine history last week.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Autumn Elegy
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The trees bid adieu to vintage 2026, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Thieves stole 30,000 bottles of 2023 Solaia, Guado al Tasso and Tignanello from the cellars of Marchesi Antinori in Tuscany.
The thieves disabled the security system and loaded the wine onto two trucks using the producer's own forklifts.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: The oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano is an October 17, 1350 trade contract held in the State Archives of Florence.
A 2024 document showed the term 'Vino Nobile' was first used in 1766 by the Jesuit religious order, per the Consorzio.
Thomas Jefferson received 473 bottles of Montepulciano in November 1805 and requested 400 bottles annually afterward.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Encyclopedia of Wine - Fresh Take or Same Same?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I take a look at a brand new reference work to see how it stacks up with the competition
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Dorling Kindersley's The Encyclopedia of Wine publishes 8 October in the UK and 10 November in the US.
Editor-in-chief David Williams aims for an authoritative but accessible reference, written by acknowledged experts rather than academics.
28 writers contributed, including Jane Anson on Bordeaux and Wink Lorch on the Jura; the book runs about 400 pages.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Arizcuren, Rioja low & high
NEWSLETTERS.summ: When urban Logroño winery meets the wilds of the Mediterranean
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Arizcuren is based in central Logroño, making it the most urban winery in Rioja, and produces around 30,000 bottles a year.
Owner Javier Arizcuren, an architect, also runs his architecture office in the same building as the winery.
The family's grapes come from hills south of Quel in Rioja Oriental, where Grenache is significant and was once Rioja's dominant grape.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Inside the Wine Festival Reshaping How the World Sees Burgundy Right Now
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Experience the 2026 Saint-Vincent Tournante wine festival. Discover new Burgundy wine flavours and see how this festivity reshapes perceptions of Burgundy
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 83rd Saint-Vincent Tournante will be held in Volnay on 30 and 31 January 2027, its third hosting after 1957 and 1986.
For the first time in the festival's history, visitors will need to register in advance.
The 2026 edition in the Maranges villages drew nearly 60,000 visitors, which Volnay's narrow streets cannot safely absorb.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Thierry and Louis Germain of Domaine des Roches Neuves
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Two generations from one of Saumur-Champigny’s leading estates on their single-vineyard cuvées and learning to embrace Cabernet Franc’s green side
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Domaine des Roches Neuves in Saumur-Champigny, run by Thierry Germain and his son Louis, makes five single-vineyard cuvées parcellaires.
Thierry Germain said that 35 years ago, apart from Clos Rougeard, single-vineyard wines barely existed in the Saumur area.
Thierry Germain said Cabernet Franc handles high ripeness poorly, becoming a "bad Syrah" beyond 13.5 or 14% alcohol.

NEWSLETTERS.head: (Another) Exciting New Chapter
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Much has been happening behind the scenes here at the new 1WD HQ, folks. You might have heard the recent news that my bruthah-from-anothah-muthah Jonathan Cristaldi is moving into the role of Chief Wine Critic for both The Tasting Panel and its sister publication The SOMM Journal. As JC wrote in the press release for […] This...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: Jonathan Cristaldi is moving into the role of Chief Wine Critic for The Tasting Panel and its sister publication The SOMM Journal.
The news was announced in a press release, according to 1WineDude's post about new 1WD HQ developments.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet Your Robo-Somm
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The year is 2029. First-world civilisation has adapted to mass surveillance. Waymos and Tesla Robotaxis chauffeur NPCs between work and their domicile.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin tested CellarTracker and food-pairing AI programs and found they often miss pairing factors like style, vintage, and ingredients.
Common AI pairing errors Atkin cited include confusing rosé with red wine, language barriers, and recommending Champagne for almost everything.
Developer Marc Lewin's SommPal app ranks up to five pairings per menu item from photos and explains each choice, aimed at novice drinkers without a sommelier.
